```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
```
```{r}
lul_d <- read_csv(
  '../data/life-under-lockdown-wave2-extract.csv',
  col_types = cols(
    col_integer(),
    col_factor(),
    col_factor(levels = c(
      'Nothing at all',
      'Not very much',
      'A fair amount',
      'A great deal'
    )),
    col_integer()
  )
)
```
#Descriptive statistics
```{r}
lul_d %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(x=gender)
  )+
  geom_bar()
```
```{r}
lul_d %>%
  count(gender) %>%
  kable()
```
```{r}
lul_d %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(x=beliefs)
  )+
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1)
```
```{r}
lul_d %>%
  summarise(
    n=n(),
    Mdn=median(beliefs),
    M=mean(beliefs),
    SD=sd(beliefs)
  ) %>%
  kable(digits = 2)
```
#Hypothesis
Gender is associated with mean number of misinformation beliefs
#Analysis
```{r}
lul_d %>%
  group_by(gender) %>%
  summarise(
    n=n(),
    Mdn=median(beliefs),
    M=mean(beliefs),
    SD=sd(beliefs)
  ) %>%
  kable(digits = 2)
```
```{r}
lul_d %>%
  filter(gender!='In another way')%>%
  t.test(
    formula=beliefs~gender,
    var.equal = FALSE,
    data=.
  )
```
There were too few people who identified in another way for them to be included in the full analysis. Males had slightly more misinformation beliefs (M = 0.73, SD = 1.13) than females (M = 0.61, SD = 1.05), but this was not statistically significant, t(494.31) = 1.201, p = .230.
